content:
The test image shows a field-level view with a distinct strip/band of yellow-chlorotic soybean plants running through an otherwise green healthy canopy. Key observations:
- Strip pattern of affected plants following field drainage/soil pattern
- Plants show yellowing/chlorosis but still standing (not completely collapsed)
- Adjacent rows appear healthy green
- Canopy-level interveinal chlorosis visible on affected plants

**Candidates:**
- **Sudden Death Syndrome**: Strips/patches of chlorotic plants following soil drainage patterns, interveinal chlorosis with green veins remaining — matches field pattern
- **Soybean Cyst Nematode**: Patchy stunting and chlorosis in patches — more diffuse pattern
- **Brown Stem Rot**: Shows a patch of dead/dried plants, more localized

**Reference comparison:**
- SDS reference shows very similar field strip pattern (bottom-right quadrant) with yellowing strips running through a green canopy
- SCN reference shows more diffuse patchy yellowing throughout the canopy
- Brown Stem Rot shows more localized dead/brown patches, not linear strips

The linear strip of interveinal chlorosis following apparent soil drainage lines is most characteristic of Sudden Death Syndrome.
